quote: It would be worse than finding rabbit fossils in the pre-Cambrian.
content: Complex traits acquired in a single generation have been observed, and neo-Darwinism was not falsified; it absorbed them. Bdelloid rotifers carry hundreds of genes acquired horizontally from bacteria, fungi and plants (Gladyshev, Meselson & Arkhipova 2008); pea aphids make carotenoids using genes captured from fungi (Moran & Jarvik 2010); eukaryotes themselves arose by wholesale acquisition of a bacterium. None of this is Storm, but the essay's test for real science is that the theory says what it prohibits and falls if the prohibited thing appears, and the theory it holds up as the model did not behave that way. Research programmes accommodate anomalies with auxiliary hypotheses, as the essay's own "would outright falsify" rhetoric does not allow for.

quote: And yet they have no idea of what the theory of evolutionary biology permits and prohibits.
content: This is true, and measured: most adults, including many who accept evolution, hold a "transformational" model in which whole species change in response to need (Shtulman 2006). But the mechanism the essay supplies, tribal attire, does not fit the data. Acceptance of evolution tracks religiosity and political identity, not understanding (Miller, Scott & Okamoto 2006), and the sequence's implied cure fails: on politically charged science, the most scientifically literate are the most polarized, not the least (Kahan et al. 2012). Knowing what the theory prohibits does not remove the attire. It makes the wearer a better tailor.

quote: Their devastating critiques consist purely of comparisons to apocalyptic literature, rather than, say, known laws which prohibit such an outcome.
content: The standard is asymmetric. Critics are required to have a model of cognition that bounds intelligence; proponents are not required to have one that produces it, and in 2007 no one did. "Not prohibited by known law" is the argument the essay just rejected for Storm: evolution does not prohibit lightning-throwing mutants by a known law either, and the essay rightly treated "no law forbids it" as no argument. What eventually produced systems with striking capabilities was not a model of cognition at all but empirical scaling of a generic architecture; the theory came after, if at all. By the essay's own test, "strongly superhuman AI" was in 2007 a phrase without a model behind it, and "they don't realize they need a model" applied on both sides of the microphone.
